question: Which compound did FTIR suggest forms as a unique component of the 300 °C–300 °C multilayer urea crystal, and in what temperature range does TGA show the extra mass-loss step attributed to it?
rendered: Based on the text, the compound that FTIR suggests forms as a unique component of the 300 °C–300 °C multilayer urea crystal is cyanuric acid (CYA). The thermogravimetric (TG) curve of the 300 °C–300 °C multilayer urea crystallization exhibits an additional mass-loss step compared to that of the 300 °C single-layer control group, which is attributed to CYA. This extra mass-loss step occurs in the temperature range of 200–250 °C.
